sense.text:
“The law of the Lord is perfect.” We know this law is perfect, because we hear it, and it is changing lives all over the world. So don’t get mad because it can’t change your life.

“Converting the soul”: a conversion should happen after you hear what is written in the book. If you didn’t love your wife when you learned the commandments, there should be a conversion to love your wife. If you didn’t love your husband, there should be a conversion to love your husband. Don’t go home and keep arguing and then say we have to fix it.

People come in with marriages already failed, broken and destroyed. They are given the instructions and the commandments, and then they blame us and make videos. Show us a church, a ministry, a preacher that is saving marriages with book, chapter and verse. There was no church pulling those scriptures and sitting people down to show them the rights and the wrongs, the dos and the don’ts. Nowhere in the scripture was any of the prophets a referee in a marriage. When Christ was called to interfere in a matter between family, he said who made me the judge.

“The testimony of the Lord is sure”: a sure testimony, because people are waking up all over the world. “Making wise the simple.” If you want to stay simple after you have heard the commandments, the commandments did not work for you, and there is nothing more we can do for you from there.

Every verse here is about death: what happens when we die. Job was catching hell. He lost his businesses, his children’s homes, his children’s lives, his health. He lost everything.

“Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Why wasn’t I born dead? A stillbirth, they call it.

“Why did the knees prevent me?” When a baby is born, the mother rocks the baby, stimulating it, continuously rocking. “Or why the breasts that I should suck?” The baby has to suckle the breast to stay nourished.
Had he died before he was born, he says, “should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest.”

Notice who is at rest: “kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves”, “Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver.” Kings have died, counsellors have died, princes have died, and they are all at rest.
“Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been”: that is the stillborn, “as infants which never saw light.”
“There the wicked cease from troubling.” Notice that: in death even the wicked cease from troubling. “And there the weary be at rest.”
Even in death “the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.”

“The small and great are there”: the small of the nations and the great of the nations. “And the servant is free from his master.”

From verse 11 down to 19 Job is saying that when everybody dies, they are at rest. There is no torment, no arguing, no oppression, no weariness. Everybody is at rest.

“Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same”: Christ took part of the same flesh and blood that we have, like you and me.

“That through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil.” Through Christ’s death, his sacrifice, he destroyed the power of the devil.

“And deliver them”: that is the believers, the men and women that have faith in Christ, “who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.”

The death he is talking about is not the regular death. People have been continuously dying, so it cannot be that. The death here is the eternal death, the condemnation death.

precepts.why:
“Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before thee, and that come after; for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.” Death is a sentence on all flesh. Everyone before us died, and everyone after us will.

So when Hebrews says Christ delivers them “who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage”, it cannot be the regular death, because that sentence is still on all flesh, believers too. The death Christ delivers us from is the eternal death, the condemnation.

“So when this corruptible”, this body we are living in, “shall have put on incorruption”: that is when we are changed, transformed. “And this mortal shall have put on immortality”: there is a time for this. There is a time coming when corruptible shall put on incorruption and mortality shall put on immortality. We have not reached that point yet; that point comes when Christ returns. Then, at the transformation, “shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.”

“O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? The sting of death is sin.” What causes death is sin, and sin has encompassed the earth and everybody on it. “And the strength of sin is the law”: what gives sin its strength is God’s law. Thou shalt have no other gods before me; thou shalt not make any graven image to bow down and worship; thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; remember the sabbath day to keep it holy; honour thy father and thy mother; thou shalt not kill, commit adultery, steal, and so on. Because we have broken those laws, and not just the Israelites but everybody on the planet, death has come, starting first and foremost with the seed of the righteous.

If there were no law, there would be no need to fear death; we would have lived forever from the time of Adam. But there is law. Worshipping Allah and Buddha and Jesus breaks it. Cursing your father and mother breaks it. There are laws in action in the spirit realm, and we consistently break them.

“But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.” We know we have the victory over death through Christ, because in time our corruptible body will be transformed into incorruption and our mortal body into immortal. That is how through death Christ destroyed him that had the power of death.

“All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.” When he resurrected, Christ let the disciples know, and lets us know, that all power is given to him, that God power. He got it all back. The one who through death destroyed him that had the power of death now holds all power.

“He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me”: him that sent him is the Father. That man “hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation.” That condemnation is the eternal death, the death Paul has been talking about: the wages of sin is death. It is not talking about a stroke or a heart attack somebody had. This death is the condemnation death.

“But is passed from death unto life.” That is what we have to look forward to, and that is why our faith is paramount: without faith it is impossible to please God.

So what about hell? We just read in Job that when you die you are at peace, so when does the torment come? Christ says, “I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.”

That death is not the regular death, which has happened continuously from the time of Adam. It is the condemnation death. Christ has the keys of hell and torment: he controls that. That is the death he is warning us about, and that is the power of death he took from the devil.

sense.text:
Daniel 12 says what we read in John 5. “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people.” Michael the archangel doesn’t stand for everybody. He only stands for the children of thy people, Daniel’s people, the Israelites. “And there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation”: that time of trouble is Armageddon.

“And at that time thy people shall be delivered”: not all races, not the Philistines and the Jebusites. Thy people. But which ones, because there are a lot of Israelites? “Every one that shall be found written in the book”: the book of life. That lets us know all of us ain’t in that book. All twelve tribes are there, but not every Israelite. Some of us ain’t right, can’t get right, don’t want to be right.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake.” Awake from what? From rest. Everybody is at rest; that is what Job 3 showed. “Some to everlasting life”: we are going to get the kingdom, mortal turned into immortal, corruption into incorruption. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt.” That is what Christ said in John 5: some of you are going to wake from rest and be cast into hell, and that hell is the lake of fire.

Some camps teach that you can be evil and die, and when Christ returns you will regenerate and come back righteous. The scripture they use for that is Romans 11, where it says so all Israel shall be saved. That contradicts Daniel 12:2, where some are resurrected to everlasting life and some to shame and contempt. When Paul says all Israel shall be saved, it means all twelve tribes, because the teaching at that time was that the northern kingdom was no longer God’s people. Paul was saying the northern kingdom is going to leave that Gentile state and become one again, as Christ wanted. It does not mean you can be wicked and still get the kingdom, like the old school Israelite camps were teaching.

precepts.why:
Christ says it: he that heareth my word and believeth on him that sent me “shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.” Then: “Marvel not at this”: don’t be shocked at what I just said, “for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice.” The graves are the chambers of death where all souls rest.

“And shall come forth; they that have done good”: those that kept the commandments in the faith of Christ, “unto the resurrection of life.” That is the everlasting life of Daniel 12. “And they that have done evil”: you break the commandments, you don’t have faith in Christ, “unto the resurrection of damnation.” That is the shame and everlasting contempt of Daniel 12:2. The wicked do not die and come back righteous. They come back to damnation.

“And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed.” In order for us to be saved we must have works, that is the commandments, and faith, that is in Christ. Be mindful of the brothers and sisters who have been in this body three, four, five, eight years and have no works, who do nothing and want to be part of nothing. Those are idle spirits. If they do nothing here, they do nothing at home, and if you marry one, watch all kind of hell break loose in the house.

Those with works and faith “Shall be preserved from the said perils”, the said dangers, “and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders”, because we are going to be in the wilderness, “for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning”: before the creation of the world.

“Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways.” Some men and women have the opportunity, but they abuse God’s ways: I got grace in Christ, I got grace in Yahawashi, so to hell with those laws. The Lord sees you, and you better fear the Lord. “And they that have cast them away despitefully”, cast away God’s laws, “shall dwell in torments.” That is Daniel 12:2. That is John 5:24 and 29, saying the same thing. There are groups that say there is no torment when Christ returns. Oh, there is going to be torment.

“For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”: like the church system that gets financial benefits and all kinds of benefits, and says you don’t have to keep his laws, they are done away with. “And they that have lothed my law”: that is the key. There are Israelite camps right now that hate the law; when we talk about the law they say F that law stuff. You know who you are, and the Lord does too. “While they had yet liberty”, as you have liberty right now, “and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it.” The place of repentance is open to you now, and all we can do is warn the men and women in those foolish congregations.

“The same must know it after death by pain.” Not right now, because right now when you die you are at rest. But when Christ returns with the keys of hell and of death, he is going to raise some up to everlasting life and some to everlasting condemnation.

sense.text: “And whosoever shall offend one of these little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone”, a huge rock, “were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.”

“And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off.” It doesn’t mean literally cut off your hand. The hand that offends you is somebody close to you: your wife, your husband, your son, your daughter, a friend, your mother or father.

“It is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell”: better to lose that hand, lose your friend, lose your spouse, lose your child, than to go into hell. And he explains the hell: “into the fire that never shall be quenched.” No camp has explained that. They say there is no hell, no destruction, no eternal condemnation. Then what is that? That is the condemnation Christ was talking about, and the condemnation Daniel was talking about.

An example of offence: an Israelite camp teaching that it is okay to go out and buy prostitutes, because many of our forefathers dealt with them. That is an offence, and the Bible says cut that person off. Bro, you got to go; you and me can’t hang out no more, because you are trying to keep me in that lifestyle.
“Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.” That worm is your soul: where their soul dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

“And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off.” Your foot is still your spouse, your mother, your father, your son or daughter, or your friend which is as your own soul. “It is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched.”

He is reiterating it, in case you don’t understand how important this is: you have friends, associates, family members who are keeping you in sin. Cut them off, because if you don’t, you will enter into that fire that never shall be quenched.

Another example: camps saying you can punch a black woman in the face and rape her, even twelve years old, and still go to the kingdom. That is not what we teach. Those are men with Bibles, but you can’t find that in the Bible; the only conclusion is that the government is indoctrinating these men to teach that, so you don’t believe you are who the Bible says you are. Where is the self-control, the self-discipline? That is what Christ tried to bring into our minds. And never let it be said that we slander anyone: we let their own words speak for themselves.

“And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out”: your eye once again is a spouse, mother or father, son, daughter, or your friend which is as your own soul. “It is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: Where their worm dieth not”, where your soul doesn’t die, “and the fire is not quenched.” It is unquenchable fire.

People say we slander them. It is correction. The correction some camps give is based on hatred: a leader putting curses on the Bishop and his followers and on all the Israelites who are not with him, and telling his brothers to keep putting curses on them that the Most High may destroy them. Is that love or hate? That is hate, and the camps that follow such men will get the same judgment.

precepts.why:
What does it mean by your hand, your eye, your foot? “If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods”, “Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him: But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.”

Your hand, your eye, is your brother, the son of your mother, your son or your daughter, your wife that is in your bosom, or your friend which is as thine own soul, because they are important to you in your life. When one of them entices you away from God, the law says do not consent and do not spare. That is what Christ means by if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: cut off the one close to you who keeps you in sin.

sense.text: Against the camps that put curses on their brethren, the apostle James says: “Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.” You can’t bless and curse out of the same mouth. Don’t do that. And those of you who follow such men are going to get the same judgment.

“Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth.” We are not even to rejoice. The enemy here is the enemy of our people, brothers or sisters you might not particularly get along with. The Bible says don’t rejoice when they stumble, don’t rejoice when they fall.

Contrast the men who claim to have the spirit of God and counsel a man to get his revenge by committing adultery with another man’s wife, and tell their people where to get good heroin and cocaine, while the people in the room clap. What scripture says you can commit adultery with another man’s wife and still get the kingdom? Those who follow them and bring their families and their women there are in a modern-day cult. Paul said there must be heresies among you, to see who is approved: those with them are not approved.

“Every idle word”, meaning idolatrous word, every evil word that comes out of your lips, “that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.”

Those who brag about being killers glorify killing, and it ain’t the other nations they killed: it is the evil they did to their own people. In those short clips they broke law after law against the Most High: thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour, thou shalt not kill, through hatred.

“For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.” That condemned is the same condemnation as Daniel 12:2 and John 5:24 and 29.

And silence is no escape. If you are neutral in situations of injustice and evil, you have chosen the side of the oppressor. The churches never speak against the oppression the white man does worldwide, because they are complicit with it, as long as they are getting money. The same with the Israelite community: wicked Israelites speak, and other Israelites who know it ain’t true stay quiet. You are going to get judged for that.
“Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” If you ain’t got no haters, you are doing something wrong.
“Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.”

“Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven.” So rejoice in these things. That is why there is no need to comment or respond to years of a plethora of lies. “For so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.”
“Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit”, the commandments in Christ, “is hewn down, and cast into the fire.” What kind of fire is that? That is the unquenchable fire.
“Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.”
“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” They call out Yahawah bahasham Yahawashi, but the Lord ain’t hearing that, because they have done much evil on this earth.

“That from one new moon to another”: in the kingdom everybody on the planet is going to be forced to celebrate the new moon. “And from one sabbath to another”: everybody on the planet is going to be forced to comply with the observance of the sabbath. “Shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.”

Back to the unquenchable fire. “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched.” Their worm is their soul: that soul ain’t going to die, it is going to be in torment. It is the same speech, the same language Christ gave in Mark 9, where their worm dieth not and the fire is not quenched.

So you can play around and find out. Those who say this breakdown is wrong never put out a class from the scriptures showing what is right.

The unquenchable fire is the lake of fire, the spiritual fire Christ speaks of. Yes, it is going to destroy America, but Christ has the keys to all of that; it is physical and it is spiritual.

“And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet.” The beast is America, the false prophet is the church system. Those who say God bless America are going to be taken, and those who say I love the Roman Catholic church and all its denominations are going to be taken too. “With which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast”: the mark is sin, when they make it lawful, “and them that worshipped his image.”

“These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.” As Deacon Malachi said, that is not talking about the thermonuclear fire, because that is going to eventually go out. The fire of a nuclear explosion, the fireball, lasts only a fraction of a second, and the radioactive fallout can linger days, weeks, even years. Say it is a hundred years: that is still not an everlasting fire. That fire eventually goes out.

precepts.why:
Now see if this is nuclear fire or spiritual fire. “And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are”: where America and the church system are. That devil is all the rest of them. “And shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.” That is longer than days, weeks and years. This lake of fire is not the nuclear fire we hear about on TV, which goes out after years. This fire is day and night for ever and ever.

That casting of the devil comes after the thousand years. Not all nations are destroyed at first: those that are left are going to serve Israel in captivity for a thousand years, and after that thousand years those not yet cast into the lake of fire are cast there too. Only the twelve tribes of Israel will be left on this earth, serving the Father and the Son.

“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” Death and hell are going to be finished. “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” As Daniel 12:1 showed, some Israelites are written in the book of life and some are not. That lake of fire lasts for ever and ever: not a day, not weeks or years.

sense.text: “If any man worship the beast and his image”: the beast is this white man, and his image is his church system. “And receive his mark in his forehead”: the mark is sin, “or in his hand”: you support it.

“The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb.”

“And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night.” This is not a day, not weeks or years like we read about nuclear fire. This fire ain’t nuclear. This is God’s fire.
How do we escape that torment, that damnation? Verse 12 is the key: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

“Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.” This verse is before the second coming, because when we die now we rest from our labours. When the resurrection comes, that is when we get rewarded for all our labours.

The works follow the righteous, and the same way, if you do wicked, your works follow you. How could you resurrect and be spiritual when your wicked works are following you? That is what the camps don’t understand. If there is no lake of fire, let them tell us what it is: those who call themselves apostles and generals, do an apostle level class, a general level class, and use the Bible.

We are getting back to the dead. “And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?” What was the Lord telling Moses about Abraham, Isaac and Jacob? They are alive.

“He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.” When your body is gone, that doesn’t mean you are dead. Your eyes see the carcass, but the soul is still alive; the spirit is with the Lord. It goes up.

That is why we must have something to die for. Edom has a directive for its Israeli Defense Force soldiers never to be captured alive by the enemy, the Hannibal directive: kill or be killed. All the nations have something they believe in to die for, as wicked as it is. But our people, what do we die for? A big mouth black woman, a corner, the wrong colour. He who has nothing to die for has nothing to live for. If you are not willing to die for this truth, you are not fit to live.

precepts.why:
“All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.” That is what we read in Job 3 at the beginning of the lesson.

“Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward”: when your body is destroyed, taken down, your spirit goes up before the Lord. “And the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth”: the spirit of the beast stays down here. It doesn’t go up before the Lord.

Up before the Lord there are chambers, resting places, for you and me to go to, until the time comes when Christ says now it is time for heaven and hell, and takes the keys of hell and of death. Some will be raised up to everlasting life, and some to everlasting condemnation. That is why the Lord is the God of the living, and that is why we have to do right.

sense.text:
If an Israelite camp tells you there is no judgment for you when Christ returns, don’t let them fool you.

“The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart.” Like Elisha: he had a double portion of Elijah’s power, but that wasn’t enough to keep him alive, and he died of sickness. Once God gives every man and every woman a particular day, month, year, hour, a time, you cannot go past it.

“And merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” Some of the righteous are taken away from the evil to come; the Lord says I don’t want these spirits to deal with that.

“He shall enter into peace”: when he dies, he shall enter into peace. “They shall rest in their beds”: rest, as we read in Job 3. “Each one walking in his uprightness.” That is the part we always skip: walking. That is why the Lord said I am the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of the living, not the God of the dead. When the righteous die, they are alive, walking and talking with the Lord. Don’t let Christianity mess your head up.

precepts.why: “If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.” Every man has an appointed time.

“Seeing his days are determined”: every man’s days are determined. “The number of his months are with thee”: the number of all our months are with the Lord. “Thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass.” You cannot pass it.

Elisha, with the double portion of the Holy Spirit, couldn’t pass that time. The Lord said you are going to get sick and die; that is the judgment, this is your time, you got to go. And Elisha said okay, Lord. Paul said the same thing, and Peter said the same thing. That is how the righteous perisheth: his appointed time came, and he is taken away from the evil to come.

sense.text: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it.” So women say you are supposed to give yourself for me, you are supposed to die for me. Listen, brothers: you are a simp if you die for a loud mouth busybody woman who hates your guts and disrespects you. Somebody breaks in the door and she tells you to go downstairs and find out who it is. Let her go down.

precepts.why:
Weigh it with this: “For scarcely for a righteous man will one die.” Scarcely, meaning you have to think about it. Am I really willing to sacrifice myself for this brother, much less a big mouth, loud mouth pterodactyl wife? Some men in the world die for that big mouth woman.

Even if it is a righteous brother, you have to think: am I willing to die for this brother, what does he really add to this truth? Some brothers have been here for years and add nothing; when you see their name or they come into the room, it is always problems. Am I really going to sacrifice myself for this dude?

“Yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die.” You might dare to die for a good man, somebody you know keeps the commandments, and give your life for him.

This is the average black man: “many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes. Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.” Many have died for women, and it is all in a negative context.

Men have to get their minds right. Never sacrifice your life for a loud, evil, big mouth, disrespectful black woman. If she is getting beat up on the street and you decide to intervene, now you are dead too. A lot of our sisters instigate problems out in the world; they summon Satan, then Satan comes back on them and they want you to help. Like the woman who hit herself with a brick and said black men beat her up, and ran one scam after another; or the woman who busts her head on the sink and calls 911 and says he hit me; or the woman with a doctorate who ordered a refrigerator that wouldn’t fit, wouldn’t pay to send it back, and attacked the two delivery men. A woman that has never been disciplined, never been corrected: you don’t lay down your life for that.

Here is the answer: “Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.” That is the love the Lord is looking for: that a man lay down his life for his friends. And in order to have friends, you have to show yourself friendly. Some of you are not friendly.

sense.text: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not.” The Gentiles there is the northern kingdom, and the Samaritans is Ephraim. Don’t go to them, not yet, not at that time, because they had to go to the kingdom of Judah first. Christ did have them go later: he went to the Samaritans in John 4, and to the Gentiles in Acts 13.
“But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that was the kingdom of Judah first.

“And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand. Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils”, because at that time they had that spiritual power. “Freely ye have received, freely give.” That is why we teach seven days a week, three times a day, and all these classes are free.
“Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses”, because people always want money, and sometimes they want to rob you.
“For the workman is worthy of his meat”: whatever they bless us with in the places we travel to, he says we are worthy of it.

“If the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you”: meaning they don’t believe. “Whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.”
“It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.” They are going to get a double destruction, more than Sodom and Gomorrha.

“Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.” Romans 16:19 shows what that means: be wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.

“But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues”: beat you in their synagogues. “And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.”

This is during perilous times. We have met governors, vice presidents and prime ministers, and so far it has been cordial. This is talking about when it is not cordial: you are there because they feel you are breaking the law. Remember the mark of the beast: when they make sin legal and this becomes illegal. That is the context.

“But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak. For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.”

“And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child.” This goes back to if thy hand offend thee, cut it off; if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: your brother, your husband, your wife, sister, son, friend. “And the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death”, because the children don’t believe. Brothers and sisters write in who believe but have disobedient, rebellious children. Those same children will get you put to death in the last days.

“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.” The only way we can be saved is if we endure to the end. The end is whichever comes first: we die in this body, or Christ returns. If you live all the way until Christ returns and don’t endure the tribulations, you won’t get the kingdom; if you do, you will. So when you are persecuted, take it joyfully, and in the end you will be saved.

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.” We went through that in Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands: we had to flee to another city, another province, because they were hunting for us. And there was the island where they had an APB out on us when we got off the boat, and we had to get up and go. That persecution means you hazarded your life for the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Do not follow the example of the camps that say you don’t have to travel, just teach through the internet.

“For verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We will not have reached all twelve tribes, all Israel everywhere. We won’t reach everybody.

“The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.” “If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub”, Beelzebub meaning lord of the flies, Satan, “how much more shall they call them of his household?” So expect the name calling. When you are on a path of righteousness, when you have the Holy Spirit on you, expect the hate, expect the slander. That is what Christ is saying here.
“Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.”

“What I tell you in darkness”: the parables, allegories, metaphors, dark sayings, “that speak ye in light”: make it plain to the listener. “And what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.” 1 Corinthians 14 and 2 Corinthians 3 show what that means: words easy to be understood, great plainness of speech.

“And fear not them which kill the body”: don’t fear them, because us speaking plainly will get us killed. Right now the Bible is a great mystery, and we are making it plain to the nations, and the nations of the world are getting angry: what do you mean slavery? what do you mean we all can’t be saved? what do you mean I can’t commit adultery? They get angry at God’s laws.

“But are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That hell is the same hell we have been reading about, with unquenchable fire.

“Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.” That is how important each and every one of us is. “Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.” All of us are more important to God than birds; Christ is letting us know how important we are.

“Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.” The context, reading from verse 24 down, is persecution. Anybody can confess Christ on the internet. But let a gun be to your head, a knife to your throat, an angry mob in front of you with sticks and bats: what are you going to do then? “But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Same context: you are being physically assaulted, threatened with death.

“Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.” Christ ain’t coming to bring all families together. When a whole family comes in, that is a blessing, but it ain’t always the case; it is very rare. “And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”

“He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.” “And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.” Taking up the cross means be prepared to die, be prepared to sacrifice your life. Christ is putting you and me in his place: when he took up the cross, he literally carried it and was nailed to it, and he is saying be willing to do that.

precepts.why:
What does wise as a serpent, harmless as a dove mean? “For your obedience is come abroad unto all men.” Brothers, you want your reputation to precede you. Before you get there, you want everybody to know this is an obedient brother, an obedient sister, not to hear that this dude is no damn good.

“I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.” That is what it means: be wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil. That is wise as a serpent, harmless as a dove.

There are men who say you don’t have to travel, just teach through the internet. The internet isn’t bad, but what do you do when they shut it off? We are censored now; if you want to reach the masses you won’t be able to do it on the internet, because they restrict and control the content. The only way to do what the scriptures say is to be in front of the people with your Bibles open. And calling the internet the unicorn is foolishness; you made that up.

“It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Does anybody hazard their life through the internet? No. You hazard your life when you go face to face before the people, to another city, another state, another country, another continent, because there will be men and women who don’t agree with the Bible, who hate God. We all must get to the point where we are willing to hazard our lives for the name of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, Yahawashi. If you are not willing to do that, you are not willing to sacrifice your life for anything.

Some brothers do nothing locally but want to travel internationally and allegedly do something; that same brother, when things get real, leaves you there by yourself. A soldier who signs up for war makes up his mind that he might not come back home. When you say you are a soldier in Christ, you have to be ready to lose your life for him; if you are not training yourself to think like that, you are not a soldier in Christ. And the camps that call themselves apostles but will not hazard their lives, who mocked the challenge to go to a country where we are not and teach and establish something, hide in a corner and teach to a camera.

That is the connection with Matthew 10:23: when they persecute you in this city, flee into another, because you have hazarded your life for his name.

To speak in the light: “So likewise ye, except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye shall speak into the air.” All you teachers, speak words easy to be understood. Our aim is that the entire audience understands. If you have to slow down, slow down.

A captain with a thick British accent stopped and asked the audience whether they understood what he was saying. That he even took the time to ask was impressive, because most brothers just talk and talk and never consider whether they are understood.

“Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.” Five words that teach are better than ten thousand that nobody understands.

“Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech.” Speak words easy to be understood. Don’t speak above the people’s heads. That is what it is to speak in the light what was told in darkness.

sense.text: Nothing can separate us from the love of Christ. “These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation”: we shall have tribulation. “But be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.” Don’t worry about it: if you believe in me, I have overcome this world.

“For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods.” Paul is talking to the believers: you had compassion on me when I was arrested, and you took cheerfully the spoiling of your goods. Their homes were raided; everything they owned was taken from them.

“Knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.” That is the level of faith we all have to aspire to: to get to where we can rejoice when that happens to us.

“Know ye that our brother Timothy is set at liberty.” Timothy got arrested, and at this time he was set free. “With whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.” Paul rejoiced that Timothy was set free from prison.

“Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation”: we think if we are catching hell in this world, that separates us from the love of Christ. It don’t. “Or distress”: being stressed in the present times doesn’t separate us. “Or persecution”: being persecuted doesn’t. “Or famine”: not having food and water doesn’t. “Or nakedness”: not having clothes doesn’t. “Or peril”: consistent peril doesn’t. “Or sword”: war. Our people in war-torn areas on the other side of the world are not separated from the love of Christ.

“As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.” We have to understand the mentality of the apostles. The little Christian Bible movies don’t show the reality of what we are reading; it looks like a whole bunch of good times. We just read that a family’s home was taken from them and Timothy was arrested. They were sheep for the slaughter because there were bounties and warrants for the apostles of Christ: let’s get them all. Herod put hits on all of them.

“Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.” Neither death nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things to come, nor height nor depth, “nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Nothing, brothers and sisters, can separate us from the love of the Lord.
Trials are meant to prepare us for days to come. “Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again. Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

“I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.” Here is the key, these last three words: “Believest thou this?” Do you believe that? That is something every one of us has to ask ourselves individually.

The righteous never die. “And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?” That is the apostles and disciples.

“And white robes were given unto every one of them”: new bodies were given to every one of them. “And it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren”: that is you and I, “that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled.”

There is a remnant of us that must be killed; it has to be fulfilled. We might not like it, it might terrify some of us, but it must come to pass. And if we believe what Christ said, don’t let it scare you.

“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”: this multitude is mobs of people, mobs of the northern army. “And they shall take away certain of you”: certain of us shall be taken away, “and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” Some of us will get arrested and taken because we are idle, not keeping the commandments, with idolatrous time. They are going to feed you idolatrous practices to turn you against your brothers and your sisters.

“And they that consent unto them”: some of you will agree, even some sitting right in front of us. All Israel is not Israel: you sit among us like Judas sat before Christ, asking is it I, Lord? They “shall be had in derision and in reproach, and trodden under foot”, because once they use you, they are going to eliminate you.

“For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” That is what Christ was talking about in Matthew 10, and what Revelation 13 is talking about: you don’t have that mark of sin, the Bible is illegal, and you are still trying to teach the Bible, so kill them. “They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.”
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” The same thing that happened in Hebrews 10:34 is going to happen again.
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

This is what the ungodly say, and the ungodly are the other nations and wicked Israelites: “Let us oppress the poor righteous man, let us not spare the widow, nor reverence the ancient gray hairs of the aged.”

“Let our strength be the law of justice.” That is why the ADL, the SPLC, Canary Mission and AIPAC are involved with the FBI and with Congress, trying to twist and change legislation to make the Bible illegal, at least the way we teach it. “For that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth.” We are the feeble; they say these men are nothing.

“Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous”: those same feeble men and women are the righteous, “because he is not for our turn”: we don’t support democracy, we don’t support Christianity, we don’t support sin. “And he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law.” God’s law is what brings us all together. God’s law is how this earth was founded, and breaking God’s law is how this world got topsy-turvy, and now we are trying to change it back.
“He professeth to have the knowledge of God”: we do have the knowledge of God. “And he calleth himself the child of the Lord”: as Exodus 4 says, Israel is my son, even my firstborn.
“He was made to reprove our thoughts.” We were made to reprove the thoughts of the wicked.
“He is grievous unto us even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.” This starts with Christ, but it filters down to you and me.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”: because these white people are not Jews and not Christians, not according to the biblical sense. They are counterfeits, the ones Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 speak of. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”: because we are going to get eternal life, the kingdom on this earth, “and maketh his boast that God is his father.” God is our father.

“Let us see if his words be true: and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him. For if the just man be the son of God, he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.” This is how they will mock us.

“Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.” That is what we read in 2 Esdras 16, and it is the same thing as Revelation 13: all those that would not worship the image of the beast should be killed. You think it was just back then? It is going to happen again. You don’t want to bow down, death is going to come.

precepts.why:
The counterfeits: “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes”: why have you got God’s Bible open? How are you going to go to your oppressor and have your oppressor teach you the word of God? “Or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” One group of them takes the old covenant as Jews, and another group takes the new covenant as Christians.

“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” Both groups hate God’s instruction, and both groups cast the laws of God behind them. That is why they are esteemed counterfeits.

sense.text:
Remember Wisdom of Solomon 2, let us torture him, and 2 Esdras 16, where a mob comes against those that fear the Lord. “And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints”: the woman is America, drunken with the blood of the saints, because America is going to do a lot of killing; she is going to kill a lot of believers. “And with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”: she is going to kill the martyrs of Jesus. There is going to be a great insurrection against the believers. But understand this: the martyrs of Jesus never die.

“And when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration”: he was shocked at what he saw.

precepts.why: “And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.” In her, in America, was found the blood of the prophets and of the saints: the same woman drunken with the blood of the saints and of the martyrs of Jesus.

sense.text: “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” The torment that will not touch us is that lake of fire, that condemnation. No torment shall touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”: they said let’s kill them, torture them; the wicked put us to death. “But they are in peace.”

When you go through bad times, wicked family members say if you weren’t in that cult this wouldn’t happen to you; come back to the Catholic Church, come back to the Baptist church. Anything that goes wrong, which is just a trial, they say it is because you are reading that Bible, because you are in that group.
“For though they be punished in the sight of men”, as we just read in Wisdom of Solomon 2, “yet is their hope full of immortality.” That is what no torment shall touch us means.

“And having been a little chastised”: what we go through in this world, in this life, God calls a little chastisement, even when it is death. “They shall be greatly rewarded”: if you endure through it, you shall be greatly rewarded. “For God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us.

So whatever comes upon us, whether it is health, life, business, family, distress, persecution, bad things happening, take it cheerfully. Don’t worry. It is just a trial, brothers; it is just a trial, sisters.
“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” He is going to receive our death like a burnt offering. The Lord likes that thing.

“And in the time of their visitation”, when the Lord returns, “they shall shine”: we shall shine, because we are going to have a new body, corruption putting on incorruption, mortal putting on immortality. “And run to and fro like sparks among the stubble”: we are going to have spiritual power.

“They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people”: we are going to rule the nations, brothers and sisters, and dominate all people on this earth. “And their Lord shall reign for ever”: Christ, the King of kings and Lord of lords, shall reign forever.

precepts.why: “Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection”: meaning when Christ comes back. “On such the second death hath no power.” The second death is that final judgment, and it will have no power on us. That is the torment that shall not touch the souls of the righteous.

sense.text: “They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.” This is the wicked: the wicked of the other nations and wicked Israelites.

Now concerning our dead men: “Thy dead men shall live”, contrary to verse 14. We shall live. “Together with my dead body shall they arise”: Christ said together with my dead body; the dead in Christ shall arise. “Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.”
“Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast”: until the destruction is past.
“For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.”

“I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.” This great people is on Mount Zion. It goes with Revelation 7:9, the great multitude no man could number, of all kindreds and tongues.

“And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest”: a young man who is very tall, taller than all of the Israelites, “and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted.”

“These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal”: that is where we started at the beginning, 1 Corinthians 15, saying the same thing. “And have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.”

“What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands?” “It is the Son of God.” Remember Christ was crucified around the age of 33. He is young-looking in the face. Stop showing him as an old man with no teeth.

“Whom they have confessed in the world”: that is Matthew 10, whosoever shall confess me before men. “Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.”

So don’t be afraid of dying; be afraid of dying in wickedness. Everybody is going to die, whether at 120 or right now during the persecution, and if you make it to 120 and die in wickedness, you are finished, no matter how much fun you had on the earth. Things are going to get very bad, but you cannot give up. If you give up on your spouse in this truth, or somebody offends you and you leave, that is not standing stiffly for the word of God. Ezra commended them because they stood stiffly and did not give up. Ask yourself: are you molding yourself to be that brother, that sister, or just wasting space?

In Nebuchadnezzar’s dream the image had a head of gold, which was Babylon; arms of silver, Persia; the midsection of brass, Greece; legs of iron, Rome; and feet and toes partly iron and partly clay, which represents America and NATO.

“And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron”: the fourth kingdom starts with Rome and extends to America, strong as iron militarily. “Forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things”: America, just as ancient Rome, broke in pieces and subdued everything. “And as iron that breaketh all these, shall it break in pieces and bruise”: just like the element iron, that is how Rome and America are.

“And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes”: that is the ten common markets, NATO, the EU. “Part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided”: this last kingdom we are dwelling in is divided. “But there shall be in it of the strength of the iron”: the military strength is still here in this kingdom.
“And as the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.”

“And whereas thou sawest iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men”: that is the miry clay, the same clay as Habakkuk 2, where they lade themselves with thick clay: the nations. “But they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay.” These different nations shall not cleave one to another.

You cannot have a mixture of all races and expect everybody to be on the same level. When the nations come before the government, every group wants something, and some groups are accepted above others. The negro is always last; Latinos are just above us, then the Native Americans, then the Chinese, East Indians and Arabs, and of course the white man at the pinnacle.

“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom”: we don’t look like much, but the God of heaven is setting up a kingdom. That is why the proper teaching, the proper application of the scriptures and the proper prayers are coming from here. “Which shall never be destroyed”: this truth will never be destroyed, and that is the difference between us and all the black revolutionary groups of the past.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”: other races are not going to rule and dominate over us. “But it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.”

“Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands”: we know this stone is Christ, “and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold”: all these nations. “The great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.”

precepts.why: For that stone: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.” We are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, and Christ himself is the chief corner stone. That is the stone cut out of the mountain without hands, that breaks in pieces all the kingdoms of the image.

sense.text: “For as touching the ministering to the saints”: that is what you see us doing, developing, growing, instructing how we minister to the saints, and the saints of the Most High are you, the nation of Israel. “It is superfluous for me to write to you”: superfluous meaning extra.

“For I know the forwardness of your mind, for which I boast of you to them of Macedonia, that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal hath provoked very many.” Don’t put us in the category of the Christian church and the other religious organizations: our mission is to minister to the saints. Paul was boasting about where they were going, and telling this church to step its game up, lest they of Macedonia come and find them unprepared.

“Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty”: the bounty is the money, so we can minister to the saints. It should not come out of our own pockets. “That the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.” When we tell you to donate, it is so we can go and minister to the saints, not for covetousness like the Christian church, where you give your money and watch them get multimillion-dollar homes, cars and jets.

precepts.why:
“Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul: And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people.” That is what they were doing when they ministered to the saints and taught salvation in the Messiah.

For them to stay a whole year, the church had to support that movement. How can we stay somewhere a whole year if the bounty is not made up? We go for a week and then have to come back. That is what the bounty is for.
